native.reason: The generated Remote Compose Kotlin compiled against this module's own classpath (:rc-components and the alpha Remote Compose + remote-material3 the app ships) and rasterised by the real player — the lane every sticker in this catalog renders through.

frame.$comment_adapter: One frame per catalog, so one adapter for three targets: `frame/widget-host`, remote-m3's — a design is drawn into a host rectangle of a fixed size, which is what a dashboard card slot, a Wear widget container and a launcher cell all are. The sizes list all three; each template sets its own environment size, and the root decides the export (RecordFreeExport: Wear widget container → GlanceWearWidget, `remote-widgets/launcher-widget` → RemoteComposeWidget, else inline RemoteContent).

geometry.$comment: Dashboard cards at the single-column phone width the :previews sheet uses (360dp), short to tall; the two Wear widget containers WearWidgetContainer declares (200x60 and 200x108dp of content plus 8dp padding); and the launcher grid sizes remote-widgets documents, (73n - 16) x (118m - 16) dp.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's own background, painted by the host inside the frame it draws: a `#AARRGGBB` literal. Unset is #FF272430, the colour WearWidgetContainer gives a widget that declares none. Padding and corner radius are the host's (WearWidgetParams), so the root never authors them.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's background, filling the cell the launcher gives it: a `#AARRGGBB` literal, written `RemoteModifier.background(Color(0x…).rc)`. Unset leaves the widget transparent over the wallpaper. The corner radius is the launcher's.

propertyCapabilities.name: text
propertyCapabilities.notes: The string drawn. `RemoteText` takes a `RemoteString`, so a plain string is written `"…".rs` and a state value as the remote expression it names — how the templates bind a card's values.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontSize
propertyCapabilities.notes: Size in sp, written `<n>.rsp`. Set by size: unlike remote-m3's own text, this catalog's text is written by the record-driven emitter, which has no spelling for a type role.

propertyCapabilities.name: color
propertyCapabilities.notes: A `#AARRGGBB` literal, written `Color(0x…).rc`. Unset inherits the theme's content colour.

propertyCapabilities.name: maxLines
propertyCapabilities.notes: The most lines the text wraps to.

propertyCapabilities.name: name
propertyCapabilities.notes: The entity's friendly name, under the icon.

propertyCapabilities.name: entityId
propertyCapabilities.notes: The Home Assistant entity this card shows (`light.kitchen`). Set, the name/state/on values become the entity's named bindings (`<entityId>.state`, `<entityId>.is_on`) so the exported card keeps up with Home Assistant, and a tap toggles a toggleable entity or opens its more-info. Blank, the values are constants.

propertyCapabilities.name: icon
propertyCapabilities.notes: An entity icon by key, drawn by HaCardIcons: the Remote icon is an ImageVector a design cannot spell, so it names one. Unset is `light`.

propertyCapabilities.name: showName
propertyCapabilities.notes: Whether the name is drawn; true when unset.

propertyCapabilities.name: toggleable
propertyCapabilities.notes: Whether the entity has an on/off the accent follows (a light, a switch). Bound to an entity, the accent then tracks `<entityId>.is_on`.

propertyCapabilities.name: isOn
propertyCapabilities.notes: The on/off value at capture: the accent when no entity is bound, and the binding's seed when one is.

propertyCapabilities.name: activeColor
propertyCapabilities.notes: A `#AARRGGBB` literal, written `Color(0x…).rc`. Unset is HA's light-on amber, #FFFFC107.
